title: Define the result as `-INF` when a negative value is passed to `linear_to_db()`
body:
## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

- Closes #109119
- Supersedes/Closes #122982

## Additional information

Internally `linear_to_db()` is an approximation of `log10()`, but as the method name suggests, the purpose of the `linear_to_db()` function is not to get the `log()` result, but to get the "dB" value.

While it is correct for `log()` to return `NaN` when passed a negative value, but it should be intuitive for `linear_to_db()` to return `-INF` when passed a negative value.

This PR means a minor breaking compat is included, but I think it is very rare for programs to depend on the case where `linear_to_db()` returns `NaN`, and if any such programs exist, there is a migration path to use `log()`.
